brief.headline: Move from 100% advance payment to 30-day credit — freeing ₹8.73 L of our cash — and ask them to match Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG price, saving another ₹12.95 L/year

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the price we already pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay them ₹70.80/KG, which is 6.5% above the best price we pay elsewhere. The open market asking price for Anhydrous Dextrose IP sits in the ₹60–81/kg band, typically ₹66–73/kg — our target falls right in that typical range, so it's a fair market price they should be able to meet.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 100% advance (with tax, against proforma invoice) to standard 30-day credit terms
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's now locked in advance payments

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit is big — ₹1555.82 Cr in sales — but they keep only 2.9% as profit (about ₹2.90 out of every ₹100 they sell), so margins are tight. We're tiny to them: our ₹1.06 Cr is just 0.07% of everything they sell, so we have almost no pull on volume alone. But they're growing fast (29.7% per year), which means they want new orders. The strongest lever is payment terms — we pay 100% upfront today, the worst terms possible, so switching to normal 30-day credit costs them nothing and frees real cash for us. On price, push to match what we pay others, but don't squeeze so hard you risk supply — their profit cushion is thin.

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited
alternates.why: Already our cheapest Dextrose supplier at ₹66.48/KG — proven quality and delivery; can absorb more volume if Sukhjit won't move

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health score B (62/100) — established dextrose supplier, stronger financials than Sukhjit (D 44/100), a solid second source to qualify

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, growing capacity — a credible mid-size alternate to Sukhjit's scale

risks: We're only 0.07% of their business — too small to matter much on our own, so bundle this negotiation with a volume commitment or a longer contract to get their attention

Their profit margin is just 2.9% — pushing too hard on price could make them walk away or cut corners on quality; focus the big win on payment terms (costs them nothing) and frame the price ask as 'match the market'

We pay 100% advance today, the worst possible terms — they may resist giving that up because it helps their cash flow; offer to phase the shift (e.g. 50% advance for three months, then move to 30-day credit) if they push back
Health score D (44/100) and debt at 0.55x equity — not distressed, but not strong either; keep qualifying Gulshan and Sanstar so we have a backup if Sukhjit stumbles
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to keep growing with you — but right now we're paying you ₹70.80 per kilo and 100% in advance, while Sayaji gives us the same material at ₹66.48 on 30-day terms, so let's talk about how we close that gap and free up cash for both of us.
